Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. From its roots as a leader in SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM), AppOmni is driving the next evolution of SaaS security - bringing intelligence, automation, and agentic capabilities into security operations. Recognized as a Frost Radar™ 2025 Leader and Great Place To Work ® , AppOmni continues to set the standard for innovation and customer value in SaaS security.

About the Role

This position in a rapidly growing security engineering company is an opportunity to become AppOmni's expert on how the world's most widely used enterprise SaaS platforms are configured, administered and secured. AppOmni's SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) platform connects to applications such as Microsoft 365, Salesforce, ServiceNow and Workday through their APIs, collects their settings and permissions, and tells customers which configurations put their data at risk.

As a Senior Engineer on the Data Platform team, you will build and maintain those integrations, and you will decide what they should look for. You know these platforms the way an experienced administrator does: which settings matter, how permissions are really granted, which APIs expose what, and where vendors change behavior between releases. • 3+ years of experience building compilers or high-performance systems software, especially those involving complex resource management or optimization.

• Exposure to specialized accelerators (GPU, NPU, FPGA, or custom ASIC) or parallel architectures

Instacart's Detection Engineering team sits at the core of our Security organization, building and operating the systems that identify, surface, and respond to threats across one of North America's largest grocery technology platforms. About the Role:

You'll help build the very AI-powered platform you use every day, with real autonomy over the features you ship. Wrike’s Backend Reliability (BRE) team is the backbone of our backend infrastructure and the guardian of our uptime. Our mission is to achieve and sustain 99.99% availability while building the tools, components, and safety nets that the entire engineering organization relies on. As a Senior / Staff Backend Engineer on this team, you won’t just close tickets - you’ll architect core reliability solutions that shape how Wrike scales, performs, and recovers from failure.

Your Impact:

• Design, build, and maintain critical reliability components such as HTTP rate limiters, internal DB schema migration tools, circuit breakers, and distributed Redis-based caching.

• Troubleshoot complex production issues, optimize PostgreSQL usage, and ensure our distributed systems remain performant and stable under high load.

• Lead preliminary investigations during severe production incidents: identify likely root causes, assess impact, and propose mitigation options. The long-term fixes are then implemented by the owning team, based on your findings.

• Create scalable, reusable tools and frameworks that help other engineering teams build more resilient services.

• Leverage AI-powered tools and coding agents to accelerate development, analyze architectures, and automate repetitive or error-prone tasks.

• Influence reliability best practices across engineering by sharing knowledge, reviewing designs, and setting high technical standards.

Your Qualifications:

• Strong expertise with Java/JVM, building scalable, high-performance backend systems; open to leveraging other languages when appropriate.

• Solid understanding of distributed systems concepts, including high availability, CAP theorem, and fault tolerance.

• Deep experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL) and key–value / non-relational storages (Redis).

• Practical experience with containerization and cloud-native environments, including Docker and Kubernetes.

• Hands-on experience with message brokers such as RabbitMQ or Kafka.

• Ability to work independently with minimal supervision, using critical thinking to question assumptions and validate your own decisions.

• Strong written and spoken English skills suitable for collaborating in an international engineering environment.

Standout Qualities:

• Background in infrastructure engineering or Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), including infrastructure-as-code practices.

• Experience leading technical initiatives, driving cross-team projects, and mentoring other engineers while remaining an individual contributor.

• Familiarity with observability and monitoring stacks (e.g., Graylog, Zabbix, Grafana) and/or data analytics tools such as BigQuery.

• A strong interest in how complex systems fail and a track record of designing them to recover gracefully.

Team Dynamics:

You will join the Backend Reliability (BRE) team, a small, highly specialized, senior group focused solely on Wrike’s reliability. You use Celonis’s AI deployment tools as your primary instruments - directing agents to build data models, generate analyses, and configure operational solutions, while applying your own judgment to validate outputs, adapt to customer context, and ensure business relevance.

This is not a traditional consulting role where you build everything manually. You are an AI-augmented delivery professional: you specify what needs to be built, direct AI agents to execute wherever possible, validate the results, and iterate with the customer. You should apply if:

An ideal candidate would:

• Preferred 1+ years experience working with customers in a pre-sales or support capacity

You will also manage approximately two to three engineers, give them clear scope, and develop their judgment. Your charter includes our content management systems, telesales technology, member app, and public surface area including our enrollment forms and customer data and public analytics platforms. You will work through the whole chain, from a data source or API to what an agent or prospective member actually experiences.

As an Engineering Lead, Growth, you will:

• Own technical direction and delivery for acquisition systems, including the public website and assets, telesales, broker workflows, and enrollment experiences.

• Work directly with sales, growth, marketing, and operating partners to understand the business problem, choose useful increments, and agree how their value will be measured.

• Connect analytics, leads, customer data, CRM, and operating workflows. Make data flows, ownership, and failure behavior understandable and dependable.

• Build and improve software personally. Use AI in development, investigation, analysis, prototypes, and useful product capabilities, and evaluate the result against actual behavior.

• First 90 days: You understand the acquisition journey and existing systems, have a clear first delivery plan, and have shipped an increment that improves our users’ experience. Your engineers have clear ownership, and business partners understand the next commitments.

• You have managed and developed engineers while remaining directly involved in building. You enjoy the scope of an enduring small team.

• You have strong product instincts and can translate a commercial or operating goal into a useful technical plan with measurable results.

• You have built systems involving customer data, CRM, sales or acquisition workflows, public web and content management experiences, or similarly interconnected operations.

• You use AI deeply in your own engineering work and have practical experience building or integrating AI-backed capabilities. You can explain how you check the result.

• You work well with business partners, make tradeoffs clear, and can move work forward when the initial request is ambiguous.

In 1851, a New York bookkeeper named George D. Lyman observed the same absurd ritual each afternoon: porters carried bags of coins and bundles of checks bank to bank down Wall Street, settling by hand, a fortune exposed to error and theft. Lyman's fix: send everything through one central office and settle the net. On October 11, 1853, in the basement of 14 Wall Street, 52 banks cleared $22.6 million in a single sitting. Money between banks had stopped being an event and became seamless infrastructure.

A century and a half later, the hard part is unchanged: moving money once is easy; making it work every time, for hundreds of thousands of businesses, across every rail, is hard. Account Manager, Retention & Growth - Remote

Description
Backed by Y Combinator and Sequoia Capital, Magic has spent 10+ years connecting fast-growing businesses with top remote talent.

This is a full-time, in-house, permanent role with full benefits. You'll be a Magic employee owning client relationships on the company's behalf, not a VA placed with a client. Our clients are busy founders and executives who need remote workers to deliver real ROI, and they need a strategic partner to make that happen. You're not here to answer tickets. You're here to protect revenue, grow accounts, and turn happy clients into loud advocates. The pace is live and constant: client calls, escalations, and account health across a real portfolio, every single day, with no handoffs and no delays.

Shift: US Eastern hours, 9:00 AM–6:00 PM ET, Monday to Friday (a 9-hour shift), with occasional early or late calls for West Coast clients or urgent situations. Fully remote, Philippines-based.

Key Responsibilities

•
Guard your book of business: own a portfolio of accounts sorted by size, health, and growth potential, and hold 90%+ gross revenue retention (GRR) and 110%+ net revenue retention (NRR). Those are the numbers you're graded on.

•
Spot at-risk accounts before clients say a word. Start renewals 60–90 days out, and get save plans moving early.

•
Launch every new client fast: kickoff call within 24–48 hours of signing, then Magic's 30-60-90 day onboarding framework, with a success plan tied to their business goals and an intro to their remote worker.

•
Host quarterly business reviews (QBRs) clients actually look forward to: data-driven, strategic, action-oriented. Become the trusted advisor to founders and C-suite, and multi-thread across each client so one champion leaving doesn't sink the account.

•
Hunt expansion opportunities and make the business case before anyone asks.

•
Surface the story in the data: track churn risk and expansion signals, keep HubSpot clean, send a monthly portfolio health report (retention, NRR, CSAT, NPS, QBR completion), and own every escalation from intake to resolution.

Qualifications & Technical Requirements

• 3+ years of B2B customer success or account management experience, juggling a portfolio of accounts at the same time

• Direct ownership of revenue retention and expansion targets across the full customer lifecycle from onboarding to renewal

• Background in SaaS/tech, outsourcing/staffing, professional services/BPO, or marketplace platforms

• HubSpot experience used daily for pipeline and account health (intermediate-to-expert Salesforce or a similar CRM also works)

• Intermediate-to-advanced Excel or Google Sheets: pivot tables, VLOOKUP/INDEX MATCH, dashboards, trend analysis

• Real US market experience: you know US business culture, SMB challenges, and how executives like to communicate

• Strong written and spoken English, good enough for daily conversations with US-based C-level and Director clients

• A professional home office: high-speed internet (50+ Mbps), a headset, and a quiet space

You treat customer success as a revenue function, not a help desk. You own the outcome, so you don't wait to be told an account is wobbling; you've already spotted it, and your save plan is moving. You're comfortable in a room with a founder or a C-suite exec, and you can plow through a messy escalation without losing the relationship. You read the data, find the story, and walk into every QBR with a point of view. You pitch expansion because the numbers back it up, not because a quota told you to. When something breaks, you adapt, get the right people in the room, and keep going.

Application + pre-qualifying questions → HR interview (45 min) → 24-hour reflection period → Panel Interview with Senior CSMs → interview with CS Director → Final Interview with the Head of Sales & CS → Job Offer

What's In It For You
₱60,000–₱80,000 gross per month, permanent and full-time, fully remote (Philippines). HMO coverage after regularization, 12 vacation days and 10 sick days a year, 13th month pay, SSS, PhilHealth, and PAG-IBIG. We offer paid training and promote from within: top CSMs move into Senior CSM, Team Lead / CS Manager, and CS Director roles.

We're an ambitious, driven team that plows through obstacles instead of waiting for perfect conditions. There's no hierarchy and no politics: you can talk to anyone, on any team, about anything. We respect each other's time, and we actually like working together. Magic is backed by Y Combinator and Sequoia Capital, with more than 10 years of connecting top remote talent with fast-growing businesses and 2,000+ remote workers worldwide.

AI is rewriting how every company works, and everyone is racing to figure out how to secure it. We have, and we need someone to take it to market.

• Develop scheduling and dispatch capabilities that match people and visits to practical constraints, with clear ways for operating staff to review and adjust the plan.

• Build and debug APIs, mobile workflows, integrations, and data flows supporting field teams, connected equipment, and home technology.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote, Poland

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

* Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development, based in Poland, you'll build backend systems that help GitLab engineers trust the software they create with artificial intelligence agents. Agents can generate code and tests in seconds, but passing tests don't always mean the software works as intended. You'll contribute to validation approaches and feedback mechanisms that help agents catch that gap and self-correct while they work.

This isn't a quality assurance or test automation role. We’re looking for someone who has built with agents, run into the gap between passing tests and working software, and wants to help close it.

What you’ll do

• Own backend features from design through production rollout, making the design calls within the architecture the team agrees on.

• Build agentic code-review and validation workflows that check whether generated code does what was intended, not just whether its tests pass.

• Prototype focused validation and feedback mechanisms with your teammates, and use what you learn to improve the platform.

• Develop language-aware validation approaches, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, adapting techniques to each language while applying a shared definition of trusted software to assess whether agent-generated code delivers the intended behavior.

• Implement feedback that helps agents identify problems and self-correct during development.

• Collaborate with engineering teams to test these approaches in real workflows, measure adoption, engineer trust, and validation quality, and use those measurements to evaluate improvements.

• Participate in code and design reviews, explain implementation trade-offs, and seek feedback on your work.

• Take part in on-call or operational support where your team's ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring

• Hands-on experience building software with artificial intelligence agents and understanding why their output can pass tests yet fail to behave as intended, from encountering that gap yourself or building something to prevent it.

• Backend development experience in at least one of Rust, Ruby, Go, or Python, with openness to working across languages.

• Experience taking backend features from design into production, discussing implementation trade-offs, and knowing when to ask for guidance.

• Comfort working inside a large existing codebase, not only on greenfield projects.

• A practical approach to prototyping, learning from results, and turning useful ideas into working software.

• Clear written communication and the ability to collaborate in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.

• The ability to share decisions transparently and improve your work through iteration and feedback.

• Familiarity with containerized services; Kubernetes experience is a plus.

About the team

The Trusted Agentic Development team sits within GitLab's Developer Experience group and builds the platforms our engineers rely on every day. We work across engineering teams and programming languages to understand how people use agents, test new approaches in real workflows, and create a shared model of trusted agentic development that teams choose to adopt.

ABOUT THE COMPANY:

The client is a pair of sister engineering and technical support businesses serving the UK industrial, energy, and offshore sectors. Led commercially by their Commercial Director and supported by their technical leadership, both companies operate with a relationship-first approach—rejecting high-volume, pushy telesales in favor of consultative partnerships that solve genuine operational, resourcing, and project mobilisation challenges.
While operating as distinct brands with equal commercial priority, they share a unified mission: connecting UK industrial and energy clients with specialized engineering expertise, technical labour, and project support.

• Brand A (Technical Resourcing): Focuses on technical resourcing, engineering support, and solving skilled labour shortages across industrial and energy projects.

• Brand B (Engineering & Mobilisation): Delivers specialized engineering, technical scoping, and project mobilisation services—including offshore and broader industrial operations.

ROLE OVERVIEW:

This is a dedicated, full-time outbound B2B (Business-to-Business) relationship-building role reporting directly to the Commercial Director. The representative is responsible for researching prospect lists, engaging key decision-makers across UK (United Kingdom) businesses, and uncovering genuine operational, labour, or project needs across two sister engineering and technical support companies equally—rather than relying on pushy, script-based telesales. Ultimately, the role acts as a strategic gatekeeper who protects leadership's time by qualifying opportunities and handing over well-researched, high-value meetings to the Commercial Director, supported technically by the offshore operations lead and wider engineering team.

Key Responsibilities:

• Work through the prospect lists for both businesses and find the person who actually makes or influences the buying decision.

• Pick up the phone, introduce the clients properly, and have a sensible conversation about the work the company does and any help it may need.

• Ask good questions about upcoming projects, busy periods, labour shortages, existing suppliers, and who is responsible for buying support.

• Build relationships over time. Follow up by phone and email without pestering people or using a generic sales script.

• Keep the client contact records up to date. If a company is relevant to both, flag it and coordinate the approach so we do not contact them twice unnecessarily.

• Book meetings for the client when there is a real reason for him to speak to the prospect, then send him a clear note before the meeting.

When a meeting is ready for the client:
The client has commitments and is often working offshore, so we need to protect their time. The BDE should not book a meeting just because someone agrees to a chat. Before handing it over, we would expect them to know:

• Who we are speaking to and what they are responsible for.

• What the company is working on and which Company A or Company B service might help.

• Whether there is a genuine need, an upcoming requirement or a sensible reason to stay in touch.

• What the next conversation with Martin is supposed to achieve.

The handover should be short and useful: company, contact details, project or site, what the prospect has told us, likely services, timing and agreed next steps. The client will take the commercial relationship forward. And the other manager and the relevant technical people will get involved where we need their experience on resourcing, scope, or mobilisation.

• Confident spoken and written English, with a clear and friendly telephone manner that works well with UK businesses.

• Previous experience making outbound B2B calls and finding the right decision-makers.

• Engineering, recruitment, or industrial experience would be useful, but is not essential if they can learn quickly.

• Someone who listens, asks sensible questions and can talk naturally without reading from a script.

• Organised and persistent, with good follow-up habits and accurate notes in Excel or a CRM.

• Reliable working from home, with a quiet space, good internet and the ability to work a full-time week during UK business hours.

• Someone who wants to be part of our businesses and build accounts over time, rather than move from one short-term calling campaign to another.

• Work from Home

• UK Business Hours

• Qualification. Confirm fit, find the person who controls the budget and build a value case before you invest your time. Walk away quickly when those aren't there.

• Value-led discovery. Tie our impact to the buyer's own numbers, such as pipeline generated from social or paid spend we offset, before price comes up.

• Price. We don't discount. You sell at list price and let poor-fit deals go.

• An honest forecast. Deals move forward when the buyer does something real, and your CRM stays current.

• Real ownership of your pipeline, your qualification calls and your deal strategy.

• A profitable company. No venture clock, no death-march growth targets, and a category we've led for over a decade.

How you work
• You disqualify without drama. A clean no is a good outcome, and you can tell us about a recent deal you walked away from.

• You build value cases in dollars from what the buyer tells you. When a buyer has no hard number, you can still put a dollar value on reach and traffic.

• You tie price to value instead of defending it or offering a discount.

• You advance deals on buyer commitment, not because a call went well or a demo got booked.

• You understand the importance of getting to the decision maker to close deals.

• You get leverage from your tools. You use AI tools (such as ChatGPT or Claude) and prospecting tools (such as Apollo) every week to sell smarter.

About Mixpanel

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com .

About the Customer Digital Experience Team

Customer Digital Experience sits within the technical arm of Mixpanel's Customer Success organization.

Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it.

Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to.

We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together.

About the Role

As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward.

This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change.

It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll partner with Marketing on the overall email calendar so our lifecycle sends and their campaigns aren't competing for the same inbox. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone.

You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built.

If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on.

Responsibilities

• Build the lifecycle communication program end-to-end across onboarding, adoption, retention, and expansion, from strategy through copy, build, launch, and iteration

• Create programs that serve the full customer base while working hardest for digital-only customers, and decide where messaging should differ for accounts with a dedicated team

About Carrot:

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com .

The Opportunity

Carrot’s User Experience team is seeking a Manager, Product Design to lead a team of senior product designers building our member-facing products. You’ll lead project work, raise the craft bar through direct feedback, and help our design function evolve as AI tools reshape the boundaries between design, product management, and engineering. You’ll partner with Content Design, Product Management, and Engineering leaders to deliver products that scale our impact to members worldwide.

This is a true player-coach role: roughly half your time goes to hands-on design work, including design system and foundational direction, and half to leading and coaching the team. If you love sharpening experienced designers’ work, designing for a diverse set of member needs across all paths to parenthood, and shaping how a design team works in an AI-enabled future, this role is for you.

What You’ll Own

In this role, you will:

• Lead design initiatives from strategy to launch, ensuring work meets project goals, timelines, and business priorities.

• Give clear, actionable craft feedback through critiques and design reviews, holding a high bar for quality, consistency, and accessibility.

At Justworks, you’ll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people.

• Integrity - Simply put, do what you say and say what you'll do. You’re honest and forthright, have a strong moral compass, and strive to match your words with your actions while leading by example.

• Simplicity - Be like Einstein: “Everything should be made as simple as possible, but no simpler.”

Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here .

As a Designer within Pinterest’s Paid Performance Marketing team, you’ll play an integral role in shaping how Pinterest shows up across the social and digital advertising landscape. You’ll concept, collaborate, and execute on a broad range of creative briefs from our world class Marketing team. The role requires passion for developing exceptional creative solutions and scalable design thinking.

What you’ll do:

• Evolve and elevate Pinterest’s performance creative across social and digital touchpoints

• Create high-impact, globally recognized creative solutions that drive the business forward. Deliver work that demonstrates excellence both for the Pinterest brand and the industry at large.

• Iterate quickly and communicate ideas across various levels of fidelity, with the ability to receive feedback constructively as well as provide feedback to others.

• Single-handedly develop pixel-perfect graphic assets.

• Be a source of inspiration for the House of Creative more broadly. You will collaborate with copywriters, motion designers, producers, and marketers to shepherd the brand forward.

• Present and articulate the thinking behind your work to key stakeholders, creative directors and team members.

• Craft compelling visual stories, using key insights to “sell” in visual concepts and make our message as powerful and influential as possible.

• Leverage all available AI tools to assist and optimize your existing workflow—from prompt engineering for static and motion assets to generating AI VO and AI music.

What we’re looking for:

• Minimum 3 years of experience with performance marketing or digital advertising. You are an insights-driven thinker with the ability to think beyond the pixels—designing story-based creative while keeping key insights and test data top of mind.

• Passion for developing thoughtful design solutions that create a huge impact.

• Exceptional attention to detail. You are a master of craft, composition, layout, imagery, typography, color and pacing.

• Strong sense of concept within static and motion assets

• A book of work with examples of outstanding digital and social creative.

• You are on top of current design and cultural trends, following the latest news in design, music, art, fashion, AI, and tech.

• Enthusiasm for taking on new opportunities. You push the boundaries and are excited by the possibilities offered by an ambiguous brief.

• A talent for articulating ideas and presenting your work.

• You’re constantly looking at how to improve process and workflow, leaning on AI where necessary.

• You have excellent written, verbal and visual communication skills.

• Experience working quickly and efficiently. You have the ability to address and prioritize multiple projects at once.

Headquarters: Remote, Germany

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Team:

Celonis grew up with the private sector: Deutsche Telekom, Mercedes-Benz, Uniper and three quarters of the DAX companies rely on Celonis Process Intelligence. Now we are taking the next big step in Germany: scaling our business with the public sector. To make this happen, Celonis is investing heavily through 2029 in its German public sector business.

Over the past year, we have built our Public Sector team from the ground up. Today, a strong go-to-market core team of Account Executives and Value Engineers is in place, working with federal and state-level institutions.

The police are one of our primary target organizations in the public sector. Police officers spend a large proportion of their time on data work and comparatively little on the actual investigation. We want to turn that around. With our new police solution, Metropolis, we help police authorities connect and make sense of their data, so that officers can focus on what matters most: solving cases and keeping people safe .

To address this, we are now complementing our existing Public Sector team with a highly specialized Account Executive who brings first-hand experience from inside the organization we serve: the Police .

The Role:

This is not a typical Account Executive role. You bring the perspective of someone who knows police work from the inside: how investigations really run, where time is lost in data work, and how decisions are made and budgets are approved. You will use this credibility to build trusted relationships with police authorities at federal and state level and position Celonis as a long-term partner for their digital transformation.

Working closely with our Public Sector AEs, Value Engineers and product experts, you will translate the operational reality of police work into compelling use cases, contribute to the creation of solution blueprints, drive opportunities from first conversation to signed contract, and help shape how Celonis enters and grows in this market.

The Work you'll do:

• Build and own relationships with police authorities at federal and state level, e.g. Bundespolizei, Bundeskriminalamt (BKA), Landeskriminalämter (LKA), Landespolizeien and the responsible Interior Ministries .

• Engage with decision-makers from police leadership, investigation units, IT and digitalization departments, and procurement

• Translate investigators' daily challenges into concrete, AI-enabled use cases for Celonis and Metropolis, with measurable impact (e.g. time saved per case, faster case processing).

• Bring the voice of the police into Celonis: share insights with our product, marketing and value engineering teams to sharpen our offering.

• Own an individual revenue target and drive complex, long sales cycles to a successful close.

• Navigate public procurement and tender processes (e.g. VgV, VSVgV, UVgO, framework agreements) together with our partners and internal experts.

• Work closely with partners such as consulting firms, system integrators and public IT service providers.

• Represent Celonis at public sector events, conferences and police-specific forums.

The qualifications you need:

• Several years of professional experience within the German police (federal or state level), ideally in a leadership role and/or in an area close to investigations, criminal analysis, IT, digitalization or organizational development.

• A solid network within the police landscape and a deep understanding of how police authorities and Interior Ministries are organized, how decisions are made and how budgets are planned.

• First-hand understanding of the data challenges in police work, e.g. case management, evidence and data analysis, and cross-agency information sharing.

• A strong interest in moving into a commercial, customer-facing role. Prior experience in sales, business development or consulting is a plus, but not a must. We will support your onboarding into the sales role.

About the Organization

Millions of Americans feel politically homeless and left out of the two-party structure. Too many electoral choices are settled before most voters have a meaningful say, and our political system consistently fails to address the nation's biggest challenges. We are a stealth team building an ambitious cross-partisan political venture to make American democracy more open, competitive, and responsive. We will build the infrastructure to effectively challenge the two-party political establishment, and create fundamentally new pathways to elected office and engaged citizen participation.

Our first major initiative will launch publicly in spring 2027 with the objective of materially influencing the 2028 national election cycle. This project will combine the scale of a mainstream consumer technology product, the reach of a modern media operation, and the ground game of a national political campaign - complete with digital and IRL field organizing across dozens of states - to engage tens of millions of Americans and build a constituency that outlasts this election cycle.

Our leadership team has raised and deployed over $100M toward democracy reform, winning dozens of state and local reform campaigns. Backed by seed funding from prominent investors and a cross-partisan board of civic leaders and company-builders, we are now assembling a multidisciplinary operating team of technologists, storytellers, politicos, and operators to build it from the ground up.

About the Role

You are a rare growth leader who understands brand, narrative, and how the modern attention economy works - and you believe deeply in the American political experiment, with conviction that more political competition is needed for a more productive, representative government. As our Chief Growth Officer , you will champion and grow a new civic platform that millions of Americans will join to inform themselves, deliberate together, and make their voices heard in the 2028 election cycle. You will own the full stack of brand, narrative & communications, and growth marketing to grow user adoption and engagement, and you'll do it while political adversaries work to turn our mission into a punching bag. jobs.description:
Headquarters: Montreal, Quebec, Canada

URL: https://www.sweatpantsagency.com/

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

•
Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.

•
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.

•
Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.

•
Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.

•
Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.

•
Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.

•
Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.

•
Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.

•
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.

Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

About JetBrains

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

What you’ll do

The US is our largest market, and we already have a strong customer base here. Now, we need to build a more focused, relationship-driven field marketing presence to drive our next phase of B2B growth. You’ll take the lead on shaping this approach from the ground up. Working closely with our US Sales and global marketing teams, you’ll design programs that engage enterprise decision-makers and strengthen strategic customer relationships. You’ll have the autonomy to prioritize target accounts and geographic markets, activating agencies and partners to scale your execution across the country.

Day to day, you will:

• Partner with Sales to map out target accounts, industries, and regional priorities, turning global strategies into focused US programs.

• Design and run executive roundtables, customer events, and industry programs that bring senior technology leaders together.

• Select and manage a network of agencies, event organizers, and partners to help execute your strategy across the US.

• Collaborate with global account-based marketing (ABM) teams to generate qualified leads and build meaningful business opportunities.

• Translate our broader narrative around agentic software development into relevant field initiatives that resonate with enterprise tech leaders.

What you’ll bring

• An entrepreneurial mindset. You are comfortable building programs from scratch and navigating ambiguity.

• A hands-on approach to your work. You take ownership of the strategy while also handling the details.

• Proven success in US B2B field marketing, ideally within enterprise software or SaaS.

What success looks like

In your first few months, you’ll establish strong alignment with US Sales and global marketing, identifying key regional priorities. About Sezzle:

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

The Opportunity

Sezzle is building the next generation of consumer savings by connecting millions of engaged shoppers with exclusive offers from the world's leading consumer brands.

We're looking for an exceptional business development executive with deep relationships across the consumer packaged goods (CPG) industry to establish Sezzle as a preferred strategic partner for brand-funded offers, discounts, cashback promotions, product launches, and shopper marketing initiatives.

This is a highly external, relationship-driven role. Success will be measured by your ability to open doors, build executive relationships, negotiate strategic partnerships, and develop a robust pipeline of compelling offers that create meaningful savings for Sezzle users while driving measurable sales for our brand partners.

Unlike many partnership roles, this position is focused primarily on originating opportunities—not managing existing accounts or operating a large internal organization. If you have spent years building trusted relationships across Fortune 500 CPG companies and love creating win-win commercial partnerships, we'd love to meet you.

Why This Role Matters

Sezzle reaches millions of highly engaged consumers during one of the most influential moments in commerce—the purchase decision.

Our payment platform, purchase insights, and growing consumer ecosystem create a unique opportunity for brands to influence shopping behavior, drive measurable incremental sales, and deliver exclusive savings directly to consumers.

You'll play a foundational role in building a new growth engine for Sezzle while helping consumers save money every day.

What You'll Do

Strategic Business Development (50%)

• Develop executive relationships with senior leaders across Fortune 500 CPG companies.

• Serve as Sezzle's primary ambassador within the CPG and shopper marketing ecosystem.

• Identify and cultivate new partnership opportunities that create value for consumers, brands, and Sezzle.

• Build and maintain a multi-year pipeline of strategic partnerships.

• Represent Sezzle at major industry events.

• Educate CPG executives on Sezzle's audience, purchase insights, and measurable outcomes.

• Identify emerging trends across shopper marketing, retail media, loyalty, and promotional marketing.

Partnership Development & Deal Execution (35%)

• Source and negotiate exclusive discounts, cashback offers, product launches, sampling campaigns, and promotional partnerships.

• Structure creative commercial agreements aligned with brand objectives and consumer value.

Cadence is the clinical AI company automating the treatment of chronic disease. Its Clinical Intelligence takes on the routine, high-volume work of chronic care – monitoring patients, surfacing risks, and coordinating action – so clinicians can focus on the decisions that require them. Grounded in partnerships with more than 20 leading health systems, deep EMR integrations, dedicated medical group, and experience serving a population of more than 100,000 patients, the system learns from real-world care delivery, improving as it scales. Cadence has been recognized by TIME as one of the Top 100 HealthTech Companies and by LinkedIn as a Top Startup (#4, 2025).

The Role

We’re hiring a Clinical Navigator (Medical Assistant) to deliver virtual chronic care support for Medicare patients enrolled in Cadence care programs.

Clinical Navigators deliver proactive, patient-centered outreach and follow-through. Depending on program needs, this role includes structured patient check-ins, coaching and goal-setting, care coordination to close gaps in care, and addressing barriers such as access to resources, transportation, or medication refills. Clinical Navigators document patient interactions in the Cadence platform and collaborate closely with the clinical team to escalate concerns and coordinate next steps, ensuring patients feel supported, informed, and engaged throughout their care journey.

Schedule

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States. Standard working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8am to 5pm or 9am to 6pm in your local time zone.

What You’ll Do

• Conduct outbound telephonic patient outreach and provide one-on-one coaching and support to patients managing chronic conditions, including but not limited to type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease.

• Help patients execute personalized care plans and achieve their goals by providing education and coaching focused on behavior modification, nutrition, physical activity, and self-management strategies using evidence-based techniques such as motivational interviewing and SMART goals.

• Conduct comprehensive assessments of patients' health status, lifestyle behaviors, nutritional habits, and readiness to change.

• Educate patients on disease management, medication adherence, symptom recognition, and prevention strategies, and execute care delivery tasks in accordance with Cadence clinical policies and established protocols, under appropriate clinical supervision.

• Monitor patients' progress, adherence to treatment plans, and health outcomes through regular check-ins and remote monitoring tools.

• Document patient interactions, outcomes, and follow-up plans in the Cadence platform; identify barriers to care (including social needs) and connect patients with resources or internal support pathways.

• Collaborate in real time with clinicians and patient support teams using tools such as our Cadence Platform, Google Workspace, and Slack, and contribute feedback to improve workflows in a fast-moving, change-oriented environment.

These responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by personnel assigned to this job classification. They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of job duties performed by personnel in this classification. Other job related duties may be assigned by management.

Who You Are

• A clinician who thrives at the intersection of rigorous care standards and a care delivery model that is still being built.

• Skilled in patient education, coaching, and care coordination - you meet patients where they are in life, considering their age, lifestyle, and diet.

• Disciplined in documentation and follow-through, with the attention to detail required for accurate clinical records in a remote environment.

• Reliable and consistent in schedule adherence, with the interpersonal communication skills to build trust with patients over the phone.

• Comfortable working independently in a remote, fast-paced environment with evolving workflows, and tech-savvy enough to navigate and troubleshoot multiple systems simultaneously while keeping patients engaged.

• Comfortable using AI-assisted clinical tools (such as Gemini or Open Evidence) to support patient interactions and surface relevant clinical context, while maintaining clinical judgment as the primary guide for every patient decision.

• Biased toward action - you bring clinical authority to every interaction, make the call when it counts, and take ownership of outcomes.

Headquarters: Remote

Cadence is the clinical AI company automating the treatment of chronic disease. Its Clinical Intelligence takes on the routine, high-volume work of chronic care – monitoring patients, surfacing risks, and coordinating action – so clinicians can focus on the decisions that require them. Grounded in partnerships with more than 20 leading health systems, deep EMR integrations, dedicated medical group, and experience serving a population of more than 100,000 patients, the system learns from real-world care delivery, improving as it scales. Cadence has been recognized by TIME as one of the Top 100 HealthTech Companies and by LinkedIn as a Top Startup (#4, 2025).

The Role

We’re hiring a Clinical Navigator (Licensed Practical Nurse) to deliver virtual chronic care support for Medicare patients enrolled in Cadence care programs.

Clinical Navigators deliver proactive, patient-centered outreach and follow-through. Depending on program needs, this role includes structured patient check-ins, coaching and goal-setting, care coordination to close gaps in care, and addressing barriers such as access to resources, transportation, or medication refills. Clinical Navigators document patient interactions in the Cadence platform and collaborate closely with the clinical team to escalate concerns and coordinate next steps, ensuring patients feel supported, informed, and engaged throughout their care journey.

Schedule

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States. Standard working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM or 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM in the Pacific time zone.

What You’ll Do

• Conduct outbound telephonic patient outreach and provide one-on-one coaching and support to patients managing chronic conditions, including but not limited to type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease.

• Help patients execute personalized care plans and achieve their goals by providing education and coaching focused on behavior modification, nutrition, physical activity, and self-management strategies using evidence-based techniques such as motivational interviewing and SMART goals.

• Conduct comprehensive assessments of patients' health status, lifestyle behaviors, nutritional habits, and readiness to change.

• Educate patients on disease management, medication adherence, symptom recognition, and prevention strategies, and execute care delivery tasks in accordance with Cadence clinical policies and established protocols, under appropriate clinical supervision.

• Monitor patients' progress, adherence to treatment plans, and health outcomes through regular check-ins and remote monitoring tools.

• Document patient interactions, outcomes, and follow-up plans in the Cadence platform; identify barriers to care (including social needs) and connect patients with resources or internal support pathways.

• Collaborate in real time with clinicians and patient support teams using tools such as our Cadence Platform, Google Workspace, and Slack, and contribute feedback to improve workflows in a fast-moving, change-oriented environment.

These responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by personnel assigned to this job classification. They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of job duties performed by personnel in this classification. Other job related duties may be assigned by management.

Who You Are

• A clinician who thrives at the intersection of rigorous care standards and a care delivery model that is still being built.

• Skilled in patient education, coaching, and care coordination - you meet patients where they are in life, considering their age, lifestyle, and diet.

• Disciplined in documentation and follow-through, with the attention to detail required for accurate clinical records in a remote environment.

• Reliable and consistent in schedule adherence, with the interpersonal communication skills to build trust with patients over the phone.

• Comfortable working independently in a remote, fast-paced environment with evolving workflows, and tech-savvy enough to navigate and troubleshoot multiple systems simultaneously while keeping patients engaged.

• Comfortable using AI-assisted clinical tools (such as Gemini or Open Evidence) to support patient interactions and surface relevant clinical context, while maintaining clinical judgment as the primary guide for every patient decision.

• Biased toward action - you bring clinical authority to every interaction, make the call when it counts, and take ownership of outcomes.

What You Need

• An active compact multi-state LPN/LVN license in the state where you currently reside is required.

• At least 5 years of clinical experience as a Licensed Practical Nurse is required.

• Remote work readiness (including stable high-speed WiFi) is required.

• An active CA state LVN license is required

• Fluency in Spanish is preferred.

• Experience providing patient ed

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. ABOUT THE COMPANY:
The company is a Melbourne-based landscape design studio founded by Drew Burns, specialising in native and climate-adaptive gardens for residential clients across Melbourne and the Mornington Peninsula. The client's philosophy is simple: every project starts with a clear plan that resolves layout, levels, materials, and planting before anything is built - so construction happens without guesswork, miscommunication, or costly rework.
The studio's process runs in two stages: a concept report developed locally with the client, followed by detailed construction drawings. We're growing our team to bring the construction drawing stage in-house on an offshore basis, freeing up our local design team to focus on new client work while drawings progress in the background.

ROLE OVERVIEW:
We're looking for a skilled CAD draftsperson to take finalised landscape design concepts and turn them into accurate, buildable construction drawing sets. This is a genuine long-term team role, not a one-off gig - we're investing in someone who wants to grow with the business, not just complete tasks.
The ideal candidate is confident in producing both construction drawings and photorealistic renders, giving us a single point of contact who can carry a project from concept through to construction-ready documentation.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Convert approved concept designs into detailed, accurate construction drawing sets (setout plans, levels, sections, details, planting plans, and material schedules).

• Work primarily in Vectorworks to ensure drawings are consistent with the client's existing file standards and templates.

• Produce photorealistic or presentation-quality renders to support client approvals, where required.

• Liaise with Drew and the local design team to clarify design intent, resolve details, and incorporate feedback.

• Maintain drawing accuracy for levels, drainage falls, and material junctions so drawings are genuinely buildable on site.

• Manage your own workflow and deadlines across multiple concurrent projects, flagging risks or delays early.

• Keep drawing files, layers, and naming conventions organised and consistent across projects.

• Proven, verifiable proficiency in Vectorworks is strongly preferred.

• Candidates with strong experience in SketchUp, Revit, or AutoCAD will also be considered - we're open to supporting a transition to Vectorworks.

• Background in landscape architecture, landscape design, or architectural drafting, ideally with residential project experience.

• Understanding of construction documentation: setout, levels, sections, details, and materials - not just drafting for visual presentation.

• Rendering skills (e.g, Enscape, D5) are a strong advantage.

• Strong written English for clear communication with the Australian-based team.

• Reliable internet connection and the ability to work overlapping hours with an Australian (Melbourne, AEST/AEDT) team.

What We're Looking For
Technical skill matters, but it's not the only thing we're hiring for. We value:

• Genuine attention to detail - drawings that are accurate the first time, not just "close enough."

• Strong work ethic and reliability - someone who owns their workload and communicates proactively.

• A long-term mindset - we're looking to invest in this role and grow it over time, not treat it as disposable outsourced labour.

• Honesty about your actual skill level and software experience - we'd rather know upfront than discover gaps later.

Are you a hands-on engineer who loves zero-to-one challenges? Do you want to build systems with real context and memory that do more than reason, use tools, and drive actual business outcomes?

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

GrowthBricks is a new project at JetMinds, backed by JetBrains, designed to give GTM teams and AI agents a shared business brain. Business context usually gets fragmented across CRMs, documents, dashboards, and people's heads. GrowthBricks brings that context together so agents and people can make decisions and execute effectively across the sales, marketing, and product stack.

About GrowthBricks

GrowthBricks is a shared business brain for GTM teams and AI agents.

It brings together the context that usually lives across CRM, docs, dashboards, tools, and people’s heads: who we sell to, why customers buy, what matters now, what we tried, and what worked. Agents and people use that context to decide what to do next and execute across the GTM stack.

GrowthBricks is a new project at JetMinds, backed by JetBrains.

About the role

We’re looking for a hands-on Founding Tech Lead to build GrowthBricks from zero.

You’ll work directly with the product founder and own the technical side of the product: architecture, core systems, integrations, and the agent layer.

The core challenge is turning fragmented, changing business context into reliable memory and agent actions across tools and measuring whether those actions actually drive business outcomes.

You’ll write a lot of the early code yourself, make the key technical decisions, and shape the product as we learn what works.

What you’ll work on

• Design the core architecture: business context, agents, tools, integrations, and feedback loops.

• Connect GrowthBricks to the existing GTM stack rather than rebuilding everything around it.

• Decide where to use MCP, APIs, frameworks, or third-party tools and where a custom solution is worth it.

• Prototype fast, discard weak ideas, and turn the useful ones into product primitives.

We expect that you

• Are a strong hands-on engineer who enjoys zero-to-one work.

• Have built with LLMs, agents, or agentic workflows used by real people, and improved them based on failures, evaluations, and user feedback.

• Understand how context, prompting, tools, and agent behavior fit together.

• Can design backend systems, APIs, data models, and integrations.

• Are comfortable making decisions before all the answers are known.

• Prefer simple, pragmatic solutions over unnecessary complexity.

• Have automated sales or marketing workflows, ideally with agents or LLMs.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: US - Remote

Our team is committed to enhancing physician and patient quality of life through Elation, a SaaS cloud-based clinical platform. Since inception, we've been focused on building a world-class technology solution that creates an experience of delight and ease for physicians, and that our users love.

Every signed customer agreement at Elation passes through a final review before billing and onboarding begin. That review confirms what the customer signed matches what we set up in Salesforce: the right products, quantities, prices, and dates. When it's done well, customers get billed correctly from day one and our finance and customer success teams avoid costly cleanup later.We are looking for a Contract Operations Associate to join our Business Systems Team on a contract basis and own a share of these reviews. You'll work from clear checklists and procedures, use AI-assisted review tools, and partner closely with the specialists who own this process. This is a great fit for someone early in their career who is detail oriented, enjoys getting things exactly right, and wants hands-on exposure to how a SaaS company runs its revenue operations.

What You'll Do

Contract Review & Verification

• Own a daily review queue of signed deals awaiting final approval, starting with new customer agreements, downgrades, and simple add-ons (adding a product or seats), then expanding to renewals and other deal types as you ramp.

• Confirm the signed order form is complete : both the customer and Elation have signed and dated it, and you identify the official execution date.

• Check that key dates line up across the order form, the Salesforce opportunity, and the quote (execution date, close date, and contract start date), and that add-ons end on the same date as the customer's existing contract.

• Reconcile the quote against the order form line by line: products, quantities, terms, unit prices, and totals, including confirming that unchanged products and removed products are recorded correctly.

• Verify approvals and required data : discounts have a documented approval, required fields are filled in, and the customer account is a real, active practice rather than a trial.

• Correct routine issues directly in Salesforce (e.g., date fields or account details) when the procedure allows it, then advance the deal to Closed Won.

• Confirm downstream handoffs fired after approval, such as the customer's billing record and onboarding project being created, and flag anything that didn't.

Partnering with Sales & Customer Success on Corrections

• Return deals that need fixing to the account executive or customer success manager who owns them, with a clear, specific note: what doesn't match, where you found it (order form page, quote line, field), and what correct looks like.

• Follow corrections through to completion : track returned deals, check that the fix is right when they come back, and re-review promptly so customers aren't left waiting on billing or onboarding.

• Prioritize with deal owners during busy periods like month end, communicating which deals are blocked and what's needed to close them on time.

• Spot repeat issues by rep, team, or deal type and share them with the team, so we can improve training, Salesforce guardrails, and error messages and prevent the same mistake next time.

Resolving Open Questions with Stakeholders

• Bring questions to the right person with full context : the deal link, what you checked, what's unclear, and your best guess at the answer. Start with the team's operations specialist, then partner with Deal Desk, Customer Success leadership, Finance (billing and revenue reporting), or Salesforce administrators as directed.

• Escalate anything outside the checklist rather than making judgment calls on your own, such as contract exceptions, non-standard discounts, unusual date requests, or large and custom agreements.

• Track every open question until it's resolved , keeping the deal owner updated so nothing stalls silently in the queue.

• Capture the answer once a question is settled, adding it to the procedure or FAQ so the next reviewer doesn't have to ask again.

Tools, Documentation & Continuous Improvement

• Run AI-assisted review tools first on each deal, then complete the manual checklist and confirm or correct the tool's results; your corrections help improve the automation.

• Log issues and root causes in our ticketing system for any deal that didn't pass cleanly.

• Flag gaps or confusing steps in our procedures; your feedback directly shapes the documentation and training for future reviewers.

What You Bring

• Attention to detail : you notice when two documents don't match, and you double-check before calling something done.

• Process discipline : comfortable following a checklist exactly, every time, and keeping clean records of your work.

• Clear, proactive communication : you ask questions early, write concise notes, and are comfortable work

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Canada - Remote

Elation Health is deeply committed to helping independent primary care practices take better care of their patients. Since 2010, we've built a clinical-first, collaborative EHR platform — and with the addition of Elation Billing, we're bringing that same clinical-first philosophy to the revenue side of the practice, so billing works with the chart instead of around it.

Elation Health is searching for a Support Subject Matter Expert in Elation Billing — someone who has already done real medical billing and revenue cycle management work, not someone learning it on the job. This is a hands-on, case-based role embedded directly in our support queue: you'll bring practitioner-level RCM judgment to the billing cases our Technical Support Specialists can't fully resolve through process or AI-assisted troubleshooting alone, and you'll help the rest of the team get sharper at spotting those cases in the first place.

This isn't a back-office consulting role. You'll be working live cases day to day alongside our support team, diagnosing whether an issue is a product bug, a payer-specific quirk, or a mismatch between how a practice actually operates and how they've configured their billing workflow — then resolving it with the kind of judgment that only comes from having sat inside a claims lifecycle before.

Responsibilities

• Serve as the Elation Billing product line's embedded RCM expert, owning complex billing and revenue cycle cases that require practitioner-level judgment — claims lifecycle issues, CPT/ICD-10 coding logic, payer adjudication and denial patterns, A/R and collections workflows.

• Act as the go-to resource for case swarms and escalations within Elation Billing whenever a Technical Support Specialist's investigation surfaces a billing nuance beyond scripted troubleshooting.

• Diagnose a practice's underlying billing context — payment model (insurance-taking vs. DPC), staffing structure, and prior workflow choices — to distinguish genuine product issues from configuration or workflow mismatches, rather than treating every case as a symptom in isolation.

• Partner with Product and Prod Dev, turning recurring billing edge cases, payer-specific patterns, and denial trends into structured feedback that can inform the roadmap.

• Contribute to and maintain the team's billing-related knowledge base, SOPs, and macros, and help calibrate the AI Case Assistant's billing-related suggestions so resolutions compound across the team rather than living only in your own case history.

• Help build the broader team's baseline RCM literacy — sharing real-world billing context so Specialists can better anticipate the issues different practice types are prone to.

• Track and report on billing-case quality and resolution metrics within your scope, and flag systemic patterns rather than resolving the same root cause case-by-case indefinitely.

Requirements

• 3+ years of hands-on medical billing / revenue cycle management experience — claims submission, payer follow-up, denial management, and A/R — brought in from outside a support organization, not built up through support tenure.

• Working fluency in CPT/ICD-10 coding logic, claims adjudication, and payer-specific billing rules across commercial and government payers.

• Experience working within an EHR, practice management, or medical billing platform (e.g., Epic, athenahealth, Waystar, or similar).

• Strong written and verbal communicator, able to translate complex billing and RCM concepts into clear guidance for both practices and internal teams.

• Comfortable working directly in a live case queue - this is a frontline, hands-on role, not a periodic-consulting one.

• Self-directed and detail-oriented, with the judgment to know when a case needs to go beyond a scripted answer.

Preferred

• Prior experience supporting independent primary care or small-group practices specifically.

• Experience on a support, customer success, or implementation team at a SaaS/EHR company.

• Six Sigma, Lean, or other process-improvement background.

jobs.description:
